newsitem.title: USA: RJR Nabisco favors settlement of disputes.
newsitem.headline: RJR Nabisco favors settlement of disputes.

text.p: RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's chairman and chief executive Steve Goldstone said a settlement of tobacco disputes is in the company's best interests.

Speaking to shareholders at the company's annual meeting, Goldstone said, "I think a resolution of that issue is in our interests...It has to be fair." Goldstone said, "I feel free to talk with all sorts of people" regarding a resolution of disputes involving its R.J. Reynolds tobacco unit.
Goldstone said the company "has the stamina and finances to fight on against tobacco disputes.

"If we have to continue pounding away for 40 more years, we will do it the old fashioned way...by winning cases," he said. Goldstone spoke after a report appeared in the Wall Street Journal that RJR Nabisco and Philip Morris Cos Inc were in secret talks with tobacco plaintiffs about a sweeping $300 billion settlement that would cover virtually all the industry's liability for smoking.
Goldstone declined to comment on the reports of global litigation talks.
RJR Nabisco shares rose 1-5/8 to 31-7/8. Philip Morris shares gained 2-3/8 to 41-1/4.
